Fit Standard Parametric and Spline Survival Models

Source: R/fit_survival_models.R
fit_survival_models.Rd

Fits parametric survival models with flexsurv::flexsurvreg() and Royston-Parmar spline models with flexsurv::flexsurvspline() to each treatment arm separately (independent fits) and to all arms together with the arm as a covariate (dependent fits, labelled "Both arms"). A model that fails is kept in the list of models with its error message and the other models are still fitted; warnings of flexsurv are recorded in the same way instead of being printed. The returned object is used by parameter_table, covariance_table, gof_table, predict_survival, survival_summary and spline_knot_table.

Usage

fit_survival_models(
  data,
  distributions = c("exp", "weibull", "lnorm", "llogis", "gompertz", "gengamma", "gamma"),
  spline_scales = c("hazard", "odds", "normal"),
  spline_knots = 1:3,
  knots = NULL,
  fit_type = c("independent", "dependent"),
  time_unit = c("months", "days", "weeks", "years"),
  conf_level = 0.95,
  control = list(reltol = 1e-10, maxit = 1000)
)

Arguments

data

Data frame returned by processing_dataset.

distributions

Character vector of distribution codes (see Details), or NULL for no parametric model. The default is the seven standard models c("exp", "weibull", "lnorm", "llogis", "gompertz", "gengamma", "gamma").

spline_scales

Character vector with the scales of the spline models, a subset of c("hazard", "odds", "normal") (the default), or NULL for no spline model.

spline_knots

Numbers of internal knots of the spline models, whole numbers from 1 to 3. The default is 1:3. Ignored when knots is given.

knots

NULL (the default) for knots at quantiles of the log event times, or a list of increasing vectors of internal knots on the time scale, for example list(12, c(6, 18)); each vector gives one spline model per scale, and the vectors must have different lengths. The knots must lie strictly between the smallest and largest event times of each fit.

fit_type

Character vector with "independent" (each arm separately) and/or "dependent" (all arms with the arm as a covariate). The default is both. With a single arm only independent models are fitted, with a warning if dependent models were requested.

time_unit

Time unit of SURVTIME: "months" (the default), "days", "weeks" or "years". It is stored in the result for the labels and time conversions of the outputs.

conf_level

Confidence level, a single number in (0, 1). The default is 0.95.

control

List of settings passed to stats::optim(). The default is list(reltol = 1e-10, maxit = 1000); ndeps is added for the spline models on the normal scale (see Details).

Value

An object of class survfitsummary, a list with

models

Data frame with one row per model: model_id, fit_type ("independent" or "dependent"), arm (the arm, or "Both arms" for dependent fits), family ("parametric" or "spline"), distribution (code, NA for splines), scale and n_knots (NA for parametric models), model (print-ready label such as "Log-logistic" or "Hazards, 2 knots"), n and events (of the data fitted), status ("ok", "warning" or "error") and message (warnings or error, NA if none).

fits

List of flexsurvreg objects in the order of models, NULL for models that failed.

knots

Data frame of the internal knots of the spline models: fit_type, arm, n_knots, knot (index), quantile and log_time.

boundary_knots

Data frame with fit_type, arm, lower and upper (log time).

data

The columns ARM, SURVTIME and EVENT of data.

arms

Treatment arms, the control arm first.

time_unit, conf_level

The arguments.

Details

The distributions, with their parameters in the order and on the natural scale of flexsurv, are:

  • "exp" (Exponential): rate.

  • "weibull" (Weibull, accelerated failure time form): shape, scale; S(t) = exp(-(t / scale)^shape).

  • "weibullPH" (Weibull, proportional hazards form): shape, scale; S(t) = exp(-scale * t^shape).

  • "rayleigh" (Rayleigh): scale; the Weibull with the shape fixed at 2, so that S(t) = exp(-(t / scale)^2). The fixed shape is not counted as a parameter.

  • "lnorm" (Lognormal): meanlog, sdlog.

  • "llogis" (Log-logistic): shape, scale; S(t) = 1 / (1 + (t / scale)^shape).

  • "gompertz" (Gompertz): shape, rate; hazard rate * exp(shape * t).

  • "gamma" (Gamma): shape, rate.

  • "gengamma" (Generalized Gamma, Prentice 1974): mu, sigma, Q.

  • "gengamma.orig" (Generalized Gamma, Stacy 1962): shape, scale, k. Equivalent to "gengamma" with Q > 0 only.

  • "genf" (Generalized F, Prentice 1975): mu, sigma, Q, P.

  • "genf.orig" (Generalized F, original form): mu, sigma, s1, s2.

The default is the seven standard parametric models of NICE DSU Technical Support Document 14. In dependent fits the arm is a covariate of the location parameter on its transformed scale: the rate of the exponential, Gompertz and gamma, the scale of the Weibull, Weibull (PH), Rayleigh, log-logistic and original generalized gamma, meanlog of the lognormal, and mu of the generalized gamma and generalized F.

The spline models (Royston and Parmar 2002) model the log cumulative hazard ("hazard"), the log cumulative odds ("odds") or the probit of the survival ("normal") as a natural cubic spline of log time with parameters gamma0, gamma1, ...; in dependent fits the arm is a covariate of gamma0. The boundary knots are the smallest and largest log event times of the data fitted (both arms together for dependent fits). By default the internal knots are at equally spaced quantiles of the log event times: the median for one knot, the 1/3 and 2/3 quantiles for two knots and the quartiles for three knots.

The likelihood is maximised by stats::optim() (BFGS) with the settings in control; the default tolerance is smaller than that of optim() so that the estimates are accurate to well below their standard errors. flexsurv has no analytic gradient for the spline models on the normal scale, for which optim() uses central differences: their step is ndeps = 1e-5 (instead of the default 1e-3 of optim(), which stops short of the maximum) unless control sets ndeps.

References

Jackson C (2016). flexsurv: A platform for parametric survival modeling in R. Journal of Statistical Software 70(8):1-33. doi:10.18637/jss.v070.i08

Latimer NR (2011, updated 2013). NICE DSU Technical Support Document 14: Survival analysis for economic evaluations alongside clinical trials - extrapolation with patient-level data.

Royston P, Parmar MKB (2002). Flexible parametric proportional-hazards and proportional-odds models for censored survival data, with application to prognostic modelling and estimation of treatment effects. Statistics in Medicine 21(15):2175-2197. doi:10.1002/sim.1203

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = c("exp", "weibull"),
                            spline_scales = "hazard", spline_knots = 1)
fits
#> Survival models fitted with SurvFitSummary (time unit: months)
#> Fits: Control (independent), Treatment (independent), Both arms (dependent)
#> 9 models: 9 without problems, 0 with warnings, 0 failed
fits$models[, c("fit_type", "arm", "model", "status")]
#>      fit_type       arm           model status
#> 1 independent   Control     Exponential     ok
#> 2 independent   Control         Weibull     ok
#> 3 independent   Control Hazards, 1 knot     ok
#> 4 independent Treatment     Exponential     ok
#> 5 independent Treatment         Weibull     ok
#> 6 independent Treatment Hazards, 1 knot     ok
#> 7   dependent Both arms     Exponential     ok
#> 8   dependent Both arms         Weibull     ok
#> 9   dependent Both arms Hazards, 1 knot     ok
